source.title: Failure by Interference: Language Models Make Balanced Parentheses Errors When Faulty Mechanisms Overshadow Sound Ones
source.authors: Daking Rai; Samuel Miller; Kevin Moran; Zi-Yu Yao

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how attention heads and FF neurons contribute to balanced-parentheses predictions, but it does not test neuron-pole job shares or the explanation-evaluation claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports FF-neuron task-accuracy counts across parentheses subtasks and qualitative precision/recall findings. These are relevant to neuron selectivity, but do not measure the named job shares, test neuron explanations on held-out activations, or score explanations as in the claim versions. Steering outcomes and general task-accuracy results are omitted because they do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study scores attention heads and FF neurons by how well their logit-lens projections promote the correct closing-parenthesis token across four synthetic sub-tasks in GPT-2, Llama2, CodeLlama and Pythia. It does not audit neuron poles for semantic jobs or estimate interpretable shares (V1, V2). It does not examine vision neurons or architecture and tool effects on interpretability (V3, V4). It builds no neuron attribution graphs (V5) and does not test or score neuron explanations on held-out activations (V6, V7). Its neuron findings concern task-token promotion, a related but different construct, so they belong under fits_no_version. The study does not cite either original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that LMs predict balanced parentheses through many components (heads and FF neurons) of varying reliability. Errors arise when faulty, noisily promoting components overshadow sound ones, not because sound mechanisms are absent. RaSteer, which up-weights reliable attention heads, raises accuracy on the task (some models from 0% to ~100%) without hurting HumanEval, and gives gains of up to ~20% on arithmetic. Steering FF neurons alone helped little, and the authors tie this to FF neurons generalizing to at most two sub-tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures task-specific component contributions and token promotion, rather than auditing neuron-pole job explanations or testing explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Component generalizability is defined using a 0.7 accuracy threshold; token promotion uses τ = 0.5. The paper compares behavior across parentheses subtasks and models.

fits_no_version.finding: Of FF neurons passing a parenthesis-token pre-filter, few reach ≥70% logit-lens accuracy on more than one sub-task. Counts on two tasks are 0 to 6 per model, against 155 to 1893 on one task. FF neurons generalize to at most two sub-tasks, via a dual-sign coefficient mechanism, with noisy co-promotion of distractor tokens (e.g., CodeLlama L19N11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On a balanced-parentheses task, FF neurons' output-token contributions are mostly narrow and low in selectivity, promoting correct and distractor tokens together.

record.problems: The component analysis uses synthetic balanced-parentheses data and training-set examples. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these component measurements; the precision/recall findings are presented qualitatively and in plots rather than tabulated values.
record.rows_left_out: Steering results, HumanEval results, arithmetic-task results, and overall model accuracies were omitted because they do not measure neuron-pole job shares or explanation quality named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: All: no Qwen3-32B and no neuron-pole job classification.
All: no interpretable-share estimates across models, scale or MoE.
All: no InceptionV1 or vision polysemantic neurons, no pose or recursive-generalization analysis.
All: no comparison of architectures, regularization or tools on the interpretable-neuron share.
All: no neuron-based attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
All: no explanations from activating examples tested against where neurons fire.
All: no simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Relation is set to 'discusses' only because the enum has no unrelated option. The paper does not engage the claim or cite its sources, so T6 applies. The neuron findings rest on logit-lens token promotion of pre-filtered neurons, not on activation-based explanation, so they cannot speak to job shares or explanation quality. The R3 value needs correcting.

versions.untested_parts: Does not estimate Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares or classify poles by number of jobs.
Does not estimate interpretable-neuron shares across models or scale, including dense and mixture-of-experts models.
Does not test InceptionV1 examples, pose features, or recursive generalization.
Does not compare architectures, regularization, tools, or interpretability-share estimates for vision models.
Does not evaluate attribution graphs or whether neuron-based graphs explain behavior without a replacement model.
Does not evaluate explanations written from activating examples against held-out activation predictions.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: all models studied (seven models; aggregate statement)
rows.operation_detail: Measured FF-neuron token-promotion precision and recall using a thresholded logit projection.
rows.measure: Precision and recall of FF-neuron token promotion
rows.value: Most components had low precision and low recall; a small subset had high recall; the authors report an absence of components with high precision.
rows.note: This is the paper's stated qualitative result across models; the plots do not provide tabulated values. It measures task-token promotion, not explanation quality or semantic jobs.
rows.check: The measure is token-promotion precision and recall from the logit lens, not explanation quality or job count. The statement is qualitative and read from plots (Figure 3 and Figure 8), with no tabulated values.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
